sentences.text: Based on incomplete remains, the body length of Apatornis is estimated to be between 7 and 8 inches.
The type specimen was discovered by Othniel Charles Marsh in October 1872 at Butte Creek in Logan County, Kansas.
Remains were found in the Smoky Hill Chalk of the Niobrara Formation in Kansas, United States.
While sometimes considered related to modern waterfowl, most researchers classify Apatornis as an early member of the clade Ornithurae.
Julia Clarke and Hope suggested in 2004 that Apatornis is more closely related to modern birds than to Ichthyornis, based on unique characteristics in the type specimen.
In 2004, Julia Clarke noted that a second specimen referred to Apatornis could not be scientifically compared to the type specimen because they preserved no overlapping bones.
Apatornis celer lived around the Santonian-Campanian boundary, approximately 83.5 million years ago.
The time range for the genus Apatornis is estimated from the Coniacian to the Santonian, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
In 2022, Benito and colleagues suggested that the validity of Apatornis should be re-evaluated due to variability in sacral anatomy among Ichthyornis specimens.
